_note: The Field Library (Archaeology's Library screen, docs/COURSES.md 'Course library'): real NASA views of Earth blended with real Mesa Verde sites, lidar and NASA videos. Every image is a file in media/ with its credit in media/credits.json; every video an id in videos.json; every place a gazetteer id; every source a sources.json id. backend/app/course_library.py checks all of it and serves it at GET /api/course/library.
title: Field Library
intro: Real NASA views of Earth, and the real sites of Mesa Verde. Tap one.

tour.title: Site tour
tour.intro: Six places on the Colorado Plateau, from orbit down to the cliff dwellings.

moon.say: The same Moon you can study in the Moon course. Ancestral Pueblo people watched it too.

items.title: Mesa Verde from Landsat 8
items.caption: 15 August 2016. Canyons cut the green tableland where the cliff dwellings hide.

items.title: The region from above
items.caption: Mesa Verde, Sleeping Ute Mountain and the San Juan River in one view.

items.title: Astronaut photo: the San Juan River
items.caption: Taken from the space station in November 2025, near the Four Corners.

items.title: Astronaut photo: Wupatki
items.caption: A national monument rich in Native American archaeology, on the plateau's southwestern edge.

items.title: Blue Marble
items.caption: The whole Earth in August 2004, stitched from NASA satellite pictures. It is this globe's map.

items.title: Cliff Palace
items.caption: Most cliff dwellings were built from the late 1190s to the late 1270s.

items.title: Long House
items.caption: A beam cored here came from a tree cut in 1275.

items.title: Spruce Tree House
items.caption: Pueblo people still use kivas like these round rooms today.

items.title: A mesa-top pithouse
items.caption: The first farmers here lived in pithouses, from about A.D. 550.

items.title: Far View House
items.caption: A mesa-top community of modest homes on Chapin Mesa.

items.title: Far View tower and kivas
items.caption: Part of the same Far View community.

items.title: Far View Reservoir
items.caption: Also called Mummy Lake. It is dry today.

items.title: Lidar, low sun
items.caption: Laser pulses map the bare ground. Low light makes old walls cast shadows.

items.title: Lidar, high sun
items.caption: The same ground under a high sun. The sites almost vanish.
An astronaut shows the sensors that watch Earth from the space station.
Lidar from orbit: timing laser pulses, like the hillshade lesson.
How Landsat builds a picture of the land, one strip at a time.
Tree rings record the Southwest's past droughts.

items.title: Moonrise at Chimney Rock
items.caption: Every 18.6 years the Moon rises between the two spires.
Every full Moon, Landsat turns around to check its camera on the Moon.
